'''Harrisons Malayalam''' is an Indian agricultural business corporation, based in [[Kochi, Kerala]] and a part of the [[RPG Group]]. It has a history that goes back to over 150 years. It cultivates between 14,000 ha – 26,000 ha  (information varies) of its own land, and processes products from other farmlands in its neighbourhood.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Thiruvananthapuram/forgery-case-filed-against-harrisons-malayalam-staff/article5307999.ece|title=Forgery case filed against Harrisons Malayalam staff|last=|first=|date=2 November 2013|website=[[The Hindu]]|publisher=|via=|access-date=}}</ref> 

In addition to banana, [[cardamom]], cocoa, coffee, coconut, pepper, and vanilla, its primary products are rubber, tea, and pineapple. Harrisons Malayalam is the largest producer of pineapples in India,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rpggroup.com/our_business/speciality/harrsio_malayalam.aspx|title=Welcome to RPG - Harrison Malayalam Ltd|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=[[RPG Group]]|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150617122548/http://www.rpggroup.com/our_business/speciality/harrsio_malayalam.aspx|archivedate=17 June 2015|accessdate=2015-06-19|df=dmy-all}}</ref> the largest producer of [[tea]] in South India, and is the largest employer in the region.<ref name="victim">{{cite web|url=http://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/kochi/We-are-Being-Victimised-Alleges-Harrisonss-Malayalam-Limited/2015/02/18/article2673758.ece|title=We are Being Victimised, Alleges Harrisons Malayalam Limited|last=|first=|date=|website=[[New Indian Express]]|publisher=|access-date=}}{{dead link|date=February 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
In 2021 the company is awarded 6th rank in Great Place to Work in India, and 16th rank in Great Place to Work Asia.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/great-place-to-work-ranks-harrisons-malayalam-ltd-16th-of-best-workplaces-in-asia/article35459171.ece| title=Great Place to Work ranks Harrisons Malayalam Ltd 16th of Best Workplaces in Asia| date=22 July 2021| access-date=19 November 2021|website=thehindubusinessline.com}}</ref>

== History ==
In 1907, United Kingdom-based [[Elementis|Harrisons & Crosfield]] established Malayalam Plantations Ltd. in [[South India]]. In 1983, 34% of Malayalam Plantations were sold to Indian nationals, leaving Harrisons with 40%. The following year, Malayalam Plantations merged with Harrison & Crossfield's other interests in India to form Harrisons Malayalam.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://harrisonsmalayalam.com/history/|title=History – Harrisons Malayalam Ltd : Rubber, Tea, Tissue Culture, Engineering – India}}</ref>
It was acquired by the RPG Group in 1988, and [[Sanjiv Goenka]] was the chairman.<ref>{{Cite web|title=About Us - 1980s|url=https://www.rpsg.in/about-us#L1980s|access-date=|website=RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/harrissons-malayalam-split-into-2/articleshow/11842485.cms| title=Harrissons Malayalam split into 2| author=Udit Prasanna Mukherji| website=[[The Times of India]]| date=Feb 11, 2012}}</ref>
When the RPG Group's businesses were divided between the two brothers Sanjiv and [[Harsh Goenka|Harsh]], the assets of Harrisons Malayalam were vertically split and put under two separate management teams.<ref name="split">{{Cite web|last=Datta|first=Aveek|date=2011-12-27|title=Goenkas split rest of RPG group|url=https://www.livemint.com/Home-Page/RnCjsjVissRim3biOq0vXK/Goenkas-split-rest-of-RPG-group.html|access-date=2020-11-22|website=mint|language=en}}</ref>
Sanjiv continued as chairman of the existing company, and Harsh got control of the demerged unit Harmony Plantations.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.dnaindia.com/business/report-harsh-goenka-will-list-harmony-plantations-1753580| title=Harsh Goenka will list Harmony Plantations| date=Oct 18, 2012| author=Sumit Moitra| website=dnaindia}}</ref>

The company has 13 tea estates and 11 rubber estates, and rubber factories at [[Suryanelli]] (tea) [[Kumbazha]] (rubber) and Achoor.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.business-standard.com/company/harri-malayalam-233/information/company-history| title=Harrisons Malayalam Ltd. (HARRMALAYA) - Company History| newspaper=Business Standard India}}</ref><ref name="split"/>
It employs around 13,000 people in rural Kerala, and more than 100,000 people are dependent on the company for their livelihood.<ref name="victim"/>
